newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Old Mutual sees soft landing despite gold.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Old Mutual sees soft landing despite gold.

text.p: The South African economy was heading for a soft landing despite the recent fall in the gold price to its lowest level in 12 years, Old Mutual Asset Managers' chief economist Dave Mohr said on Thursday.
And fears that the economy was about to slip into an outright recession, or may already have done so, appeared overly pessimistic.
"In spite of the weak first quarter gross domestic product (GDP) numbers, the subsequent collapse in car sales and the crisis in gold mining, we still believe a soft landing is plausible.
"We expect GDP growth of two percent this year and higher growth in 1998," Mohr told a news conference.
Mohr said although South African gold mines' problems would contribute to the slowdown in the economy, the impact would be far from disastrous.
Gold was trading at $326 an ounce in London on Thursday. Earlier this month it fell to a 12-year low of $314 an ounce.
"Mining contributes only eight percent to total GDP of which gold mining is probably less than half."
The non-gold mining sector had been performing well, benefitting from healthy foreign demand and a slight firming in commodity prices, Mohr noted.
Among the bullish factors which would prevent a recession was the good performance of the manufacturing sector which Mohr said could be in far better shape and less at risk from a slump.
"Over the past few years industry has upgraded plant and equipment aggressively in order to improve competitiveness," he said.
This appeared to be paying off with manufactured exports rising faster than the traditional raw material exports over the past few years.
In addition, the long-awaited investment revival in social and physical infrastruture could finally be getting underway, albeit at a moderate pace, he added.
